segments.title: Chương 34: 0034【Bài quảng cáo soft-sell lại viral?】
segments.content:
Di Du.

Fu Guoqiang was a born and bred Beijing local.

In the early years after the founding of the People's Republic, his grandfather was transferred from the Northeast to Di Du to serve as a key technical expert at a state-owned enterprise.

His parents were also state-owned enterprise workers.

Later, his older brother and sister took over their parents' jobs.

But when Fu Guoqiang returned from the countryside as an educated youth, he could only be an unemployed young man, and he even submitted and published some "scar literature."

When he was young, he went to Pengcheng and Yangcheng to try his luck, peddling things like cassette tapes and jeans. Then he got into pirating books, collaborating with legitimate printing factories to illegally print all sorts of miscellaneous novels.

Later on, he went legitimate and started a proper business, opening a department store in Beijing. Because the location was quite good and the scale was not small, it was acquired by Hualian four years ago and converted into a supermarket.

He also became a minor shareholder in the Hualian Supermarket company. At first, he could still manage his original store, but later on, a reform of the management system kicked him out. He could only sit and collect dividends, finding it difficult to participate in company affairs.

Two years ago, the company went public...

Suddenly without a goal in life, Fu Guoqiang didn't know what to do all day and could only drink and shoot the breeze with his friends every few days.

Until he came across Legend of Mir, he was instantly hooked.

But a few months ago, Fu Guoqiang quit playing.

The game was flooded with cheats, the version never got updated, and they even launched some "Player Migration Plan."

Some of his friends from the game moved to The World of Legend, some stayed in Legend of Mir, some went to play Legend of Mir 3, and some quit online games altogether.

Fu Guoqiang tried all the newly released games.

But every time he played for half a month, he felt it was incredibly boring, and he missed the days when he first started playing Legend of Mir more than ever.

What he missed was actually the "brotherly bond" and his own gaming years.

On Tuesday, Fu Guoqiang had nothing to do, so he logged onto the 17173 forum to spam posts and join other netizens in their daily cursing of Shanda.

While he was at it, he looked for some new games to play.

You could also buy and sell equipment and cheats here; it was hard for netizens who liked gaming to bypass 17173.

"Huh, what's this?"

Fu Guoqiang saw a hot post: A Legend of Mir Refugee's Heartfelt Plea: The Internet is So Big, Where is My Home?

The title alone struck a chord in Fu Guoqiang's heart.

"I am an orphan of the online world, a refugee whose home was destroyed by Shanda..."

"At the end of 2001, knowing nothing about online games, I stumbled懵懂 into a world called Legend of Mir. I got a new name, picked up a wooden sword, and charged at the chickens. I've fought with rake cats and been chased all over by orcs..."

"I had already reached level 10, but I was still foolishly hacking at monsters with a Wooden Sword, not knowing I could learn Fire Ball. I saw a young mage casting flames and chased him for a long time, but he wouldn't teach me. Then, I met my first brother in the game. He took me to buy skill books, taught me how to form a party, and we adventured together on the Marfa Continent..."

"At level 26, I met my girlfriend in the game. She was a female Taoist. Our meeting happened in a romantic yet cliché story of a hero saving a damsel in distress..."

"I had many friends, and to this day, I still remember their names. They were called Xiao Qingfeng, A Sword From the West, Black Cat Sheriff 123, Hahaxihaha... We spent all night mining and chatting in the mines, we excitedly went to burn pigs together, and we got lost like idiots wandering through the Zuma labyrinth..."

"The first time I said goodbye to a friend was due to server lag. During that period, the lag was so bad I couldn't function... When Xiao Qingfeng left, he said a lot of sentimental things and gave me his full set of equipment... He said the people here were great, but the game was terrible. He couldn't stand it anymore and hoped we would still be brothers if we met again in the pugilistic world. I have his QQ and we still chat occasionally, but we feel more and more like strangers..."

"Life is like that; where there are gatherings, there are partings. During the equipment duplication incident, two more friends left. A Sword From the West and Black Cat Sheriff took advantage of the bug's tail end to duplicate equipment. They didn't make much, but their accounts all got banned... Were they greedy? It seems so, but also maybe not..."

"I still remember during the wedding event, my girlfriend was so envious of the newlywed couple in the game. So, we arranged to meet in real life. I specially bought a ring and took a train to see her. She cried and said she would marry me after graduation. However, even solemn vows can be broken one day. She didn't marry me. She just said sorry and then disappeared from my world forever..."

"I still remember she wanted to see the stars in the Viper Valley. It seemed there were no stars there; we couldn't raise our heads to gaze at the starry sky... Perhaps what we missed was not just the starry sky, but also the 'don't go' that we couldn't bring ourselves to say..."

"The day she said goodbye, I got terribly drunk. I dreamt she was being chased by a White Boar, shouting 'Husband, save me!' at me. I wanted to save her, but I couldn't control my body, couldn't lift my magic wand... I started having dreams often after that. Every time, there was a girl in my dream, chased by all sorts of monsters, calling out for me to be the hero and save the damsel in distress..."

"She left in the end, and I started spending less time playing the game. But every weekend, I would log in and chat with my brothers and sisters. The map was updated again, and everyone took me to the new map to fight monsters. There were also more and more cheats, which I found a bit hard to get used to..."

"Xixihaxixi, who was still in the game, called me a while back and said he was leaving Legend of Mir too. He couldn't stand the cheats, couldn't stand the maps never being updated. He was sick of it. He had traveled to every corner of every map, yet Shanda broke its promises to update the version time and time again..."

"He said that the last time he logged off, he walked around the safe zone again and again. It was like saying goodbye to his youth, or like attending his own funeral. He said his wandering in circles looked like the time he couldn't find the exit of the Stone Tomb Array, completely lost as if trapped by a ghostly wall..."

"I logged back into the game. Everything here was familiar yet strange. My old friends were all gone, and my youth had gone with them..."

"I sent them messages on QQ and called them one by one. A Sword From the West said he was playing a private server. I downloaded the private server to play with him, and I spent money to buy equipment. It was so boring. It was nothing but PK, PK, and more PK..."

"My game world has been destroyed, vanishing along with all the wonderful memories. I am a homeless internet orphan, unable to find my spiritual home. I don't know where I can belong, where my final destination is..."

"I met up with A Sword From the West for a drink in real life. He said he wanted to create a Legend of Mir private server that doesn't sell equipment, so that old friends who can't find a home can relive the past."

"But is that possible?"

"A Sword From the West said he has a bit of money, but doesn't know how to make a game. I said I could help ask around."

"Brothers and sisters who once played Legend of Mir, are you all doing well now? In which corner of the internet have you scattered? I want to meet you all again. Perhaps the horn of our reunion still sounds in the Woma Temple, and a paradise might be hidden behind the Peach Blossom Gate..."

"For this goal, we must work hard. If we were to make a private server that doesn't sell equipment, what advice and suggestions do you have? Maybe we can really make it happen and let us relive those passionate years."

"Just like fighting a boss with low health and no mana, in this world, who knows the outcome of things if you don't even try?"

Fu Guoqiang read the 2,000-word long post from beginning to end, very carefully.

The first thirty-something replies were all from astroturfers sent by Tao Chenggang, while the later ones were from real netizens.

"Damn, this makes me think of my wife from the game. I'm going to leave a message on her QQ and ask if she's willing to be my girlfriend again."

"Shanda should die! I'm a game refugee and an internet orphan too!"

"Wake up, OP. Tell your friend not to make a private server. A private server that doesn't sell equipment, is he just going to keep pouring money into it?"

"I don't know how to help with ideas, but if the OP's private server gets made, I'll definitely log in to show my support."

"Who still remembers pulling all-nighters to camp the Corpse King, just for a chance at a Summon Godly Beast book drop after several days and nights?"

"I was camping for a Magic Shield drop. Have you guys ever seen a level 35 mage without a Magic Shield?"

"Haha, I learned Magic Shield at level 33."

"Damn, it brings tears to my eyes just thinking about it. I was still using my skeleton baby at level 39."

"..."

As more and more netizens joined in, the post gradually turned into a trip down memory lane.

A large group of Legend of Mir refugees came to the thread to vent their frustrations and reminisce about the laughter and tears of those years. Guided by the astroturfers, they each shared their stories from the game, sharing bits and pieces of their experiences when they first started playing Legend of Mir.

Fu Guoqiang carefully read every reply.

Before he knew it, his eyes grew moist.

He was reminded of his own past, of his friends from the game, recalling those crazy yet heartwarming years.

After a long while, Fu Guoqiang finished reading the post, refreshing it again and again, hoping to see more replies.

"This post has been stickied by the admin!"

Fu Guoqiang saw the latest reply, immediately switched out to check, and sure enough, the post had been stickied.

Many domestic forums started having a sticky function in 2002. But up to this point, it was still not possible to post hyperlinks and attachments in threads.

17173 stickied Tao Chenggang's post, naturally, for the website's own benefit.

In this era, a website's value was entirely dependent on its traffic.

Just a month ago, 17173 had been acquired by Sohu and was beginning to transform into a gaming portal.

They didn't care if you were badmouthing Shanda. As long as it could increase traffic, they would definitely give special treatment to hot posts.

Fu Guoqiang refreshed the forum again and soon saw another post: Legend of Mir Refugee's Private Server Development Log.

"I was just venting on the forum, but I didn't expect so many brothers and sisters to follow up with such enthusiasm. I copied the post's URL and sent it to my friend, A Sword From the West. He was very moved after reading the replies and said he would make the private server even if he had to sell everything he owns."

"Right now, he's already contacting technical experts, and the daily development progress will be live-blogged. But A Sword From the West also said that he has limited funds, and to make the private server sustainable long-term, it must charge a fee."

"Does anyone have any good suggestions? Without charging by the hour, selling equipment, or selling features, how can we recoup the investment in a private server?"

Fu Guoqiang stared at the post for a long time, unable to think of any good ideas.

He really wanted to help offer some advice right now.

This was about youth, and also about dreams. Fu Guoqiang was eager to get involved.

He even hoped that "A Sword From the West" could make money from the private server. When the server opened, he would definitely be willing to pay to support it.

Both posts were reposted by "enthusiastic netizens" to all the major gaming forums, prompting more genuinely enthusiastic netizens to actively participate in the discussion.

Two days later, this thing even broke out of its circle, being reposted to Tianya, Mop, SC, Xici Hutong, and various major university BBSes.

Of course, the popularity on other types of forums was certainly not as high as on gaming forums.

They were just watching the excitement.

However, terms like "Legend of Mir refugee," "game refugee," and "internet orphan" gradually became a consensus within certain player communities. Especially old Legend of Mir players, who liked to use these terms for self-deprecating jokes.

Seeing the rising popularity, 17173, in order to earn more traffic, even gave it a special feature report on their homepage.

For free.

Tao Chenggang was a bit stunned. He called Chen Guiliang: "This is getting a bit out of hand."

"I didn't expect it either," Chen Guiliang said honestly.

In this era, entertainment was relatively scarce and there were few websites, so a hot post could easily break out of its circle without anyone knowing how.

Especially after the pioneering move of mobilizing astroturfers to participate!

Chen Guiliang said: "Rent two more servers. I'm afraid the private server might lag."

Tao Chenggang worried: "We're not going to get targeted by Shanda, are we?"

Shanda: If you were some small fry hiding in a corner stealing a bit of money from me, I wouldn't say anything. But you're being so blatant, it would be unreasonable if I didn't send a lawyer's letter. My personal guess is that if this thing takes off, Shanda might try to recruit them. It wouldn't be a bad way to make a quick buck.

Chen Guiliang: "..."

(Requesting monthly tickets.)

(Sacrificing a rebirth novel, over 1.6 million words, already in the premium collection. Rewinding to Youth.)
